title: Pauline Jaricot (1799–1862)
hook: a young laywoman in Lyon organizes small groups that fund missions far beyond France

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Curé of Ars, the village priest in the confessional. Your line was sixteen hours a day. Who got your full attention? Today, a young woman with a coin box. Day eight hundred eighty-eight.

Lyon, France, a city of silk. In the workshops, women and girls stand at the looms for long days, for small pay. One young woman from a well-off family of silk merchants has been going through a change of heart. She has put away her fine dresses. Her brother, studying for the priesthood, writes home about missionaries far away and how little they have. She can't send much herself. But she has an idea about the women at the looms. Not one big gift from one rich person. Something tiny, from many hands, every week.
screen: `A CITY OF SILK AND LOOMS.` → `MISSIONARIES WITH LITTLE.` → `SOMETHING TINY, EVERY WEEK.`

segments.voice: Her name was Pauline Jaricot. She was not a nun, and she never became one. She stayed a laywoman her whole life. Her idea unfolds in four steps. First, the circle. She asked a small group of friends and workers to give a small coin each week, and to pray for the missions. Each of them gathered a small group of their own. Groups fed into groups. Second, the network. Small circles became something much larger. Out of this work came the Society for the Propagation of the Faith, which Catholics still support today when a collection is taken up for the missions. Third, the smallest coin. In Mark's Gospel, Jesus watches a poor widow drop two tiny coins into the temple treasury, and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "this poor widow hath cast in more than all they who have cast into the treasury." In the Latin of the Vulgate, her two coins are duo minuta. Pauline couldn't cross the ocean. The women at the looms couldn't either. But a small coin, given again and again, could. Fourth, the hard ending. Later in life, she put money into a venture meant to give workers decent jobs and a decent life. It failed. People she trusted let her down, and she was left in debt and poverty, and she died poor. The Church did not forget her; it later declared her blessed. Her story asks a quiet question. What can a small group of ordinary people do, if each gives a little, and keeps giving? Her answer reached far beyond Lyon. She never saw the places those coins went.
screen: `A COIN A WEEK, AND A PRAYER.` · `CIRCLES BECOME A SOCIETY.` · `THE WIDOW'S TWO COINS.` · `A FAILED VENTURE, A POOR DEATH.` · then, large: `SMALL GROUPS, WHOLE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give a coin to missions, or to anyone far away who needs it. First, settle, and breathe. Hold a coin in your hand if you have one, or just picture it. Feel how small it is. Now think of where it might go: a clinic, a school, a kitchen, a family you will never meet. Let that distance sit with you. If you pray, you can pray for people working far from home for others. If you don't, simply wish them well. When the bell rings, you might set that coin aside somewhere you'll see it. The bell holds the time.
Pauline Jaricot. A laywoman of Lyon whose small circles of givers grew into the Society for the Propagation of the Faith.
Your line: small groups, whole world. Today, put one coin, or one small gift, toward someone you'll never meet. Day eight hundred eighty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholic parishes hold a yearly collection for the missions, World Mission Sunday, which supports the Society for the Propagation of the Faith; some Catholics also give a small amount each month through mission societies.

notes: Claims rule: the index hook's 'worldwide' and the traditional 'groups of ten' were softened to 'far beyond France' and 'small groups'. Confirm.
Her brother Philéas writing home about missions, and her working among the silk workers of Lyon: confirm.
Society for the Propagation of the Faith growing out of her circles: confirm wording (others are sometimes credited with the formal founding).
The failed venture (the Notre-Dame des Anges ironworks) and her death in poverty: confirm.
Declared blessed (beatified): confirm; date left out per claims rule.
Ecclesiastical pronunciation of duo minuta: confirm.
Editor pass: untangled the hook's brother sentence; replaced the repeated 'turned four ways' opener; 'her coins' changed to 'those coins' (the coins were the givers', not hers).
